modules.name: Workspace, identity aur access
modules.baseline: Existing auth/team code; hard-coded privileged identity and email verification defects.
modules.owns: Workspaces, identities, sessions, memberships, role grants and service identities.

features.description: Production OIDC with verified-email requirements, explicit owner bootstrap, MFA/passkey or IdP step-up for sensitive actions; remove hard-coded owner bypasses.
Workspace isolation independent of user IDs; least-privilege owner/recruiter/coordinator/finance/viewer plus scoped automation identities.
Client and candidate identities with record/purpose-scoped access; team invitation, revocation, session expiry, device/session history.
Scoped integration service accounts, signed revocable share/calendar tokens, impersonation controls and audited break-glass access.
Permission-aware UI and APIs using the same capability registry; authorization repeated on downloads, exports, webhooks and worker actions.

modules.accept: Another workspace cannot read/mutate/export a record; revoked users/tokens lose access; unverified email cannot grant owner privileges; calendar feed requires scoped authorization.

modules.name: Integration aur provider hub
modules.baseline: Hostinger and managed-service helpers exist; most recruitment connectors missing.
modules.owns: Provider connections, credentials metadata, adapter contracts, webhook inbox and normalized provider events.

features.description: Versioned adapters for email, approved WhatsApp/SMS/voice, Google/Microsoft calendars, meeting providers, e-sign, payment/bank feeds, assessments, verification and approved talent/client sources.
OAuth refresh, credential rotation, per-workspace scopes, destination restrictions, health probes, quota/cost limits and connection-specific kill switches.
Signed webhook verification, replay protection, raw-event reference, deduplication, out-of-order reconciliation and deterministic event routing.
Source licensing/permission and provenance declarations; API/CSV/ATS import/export with field mapping, backfill checkpoints and quarantine.
Real scheduler registration checks through M05; no mock success in production. Provider sandbox/contract tests, schema-drift detection and reconnect workflows.
All domains call these adapters instead of copying provider SDKs; actual message lifecycle belongs to M07 and financial truth to M21.

modules.accept: Expired credentials recover or open a visible case; duplicate webhook produces one normalized event; an unconfigured provider cannot be marked live.

modules.name: Canonical data, identity resolution aur evidence
modules.baseline: Shared schema exists; mock semantics, duplicate handling and constraints diverge.
modules.owns: Cross-domain identity links, provenance/evidence references, merge history and schema/migration conventions; domain modules own their business records.

features.description: Stable workspace-scoped IDs and canonical links for organization, contact, person, requisition, candidacy and commercial engagement.
Person/candidate profile separated from candidate-job application so parallel jobs do not overwrite lifecycle or decisions.
Normalized email/phone/domain matching, explainable duplicate suggestions, confidence-based merges, reversible merge lineage and collision review.
Versioned source facts, timestamps, freshness, conflicting-claim handling, evidence access/retention labels and correction propagation.
features.implementation_note: W2 stores immutable follow-up definition snapshots and paginated history; general source-fact provenance/freshness/conflict handling remains pending.

features.description: Document text is owned by M14, consent by M04 and payment records by M21; use references/read models rather than copying authoritative state.
Real MySQL constraints, currency/time/amount types, optimistic versions, transactional migrations, bounded pagination and index/query plans.
features.implementation_note: W3 adds owned/versioned collection records, indexed bounded scans, fresh/incremental migrations 0013/0014 and BIGINT cumulative receipt baselines; wider data/query-plan acceptance remains open.

modules.accept: One person can have separate active candidacies; source corrections invalidate stale derived scores; real DB uniqueness matches allowed histories and retries.

modules.name: Policy, delegation, consent aur privacy
modules.baseline: Approval and consent code exists; inconsistent paths, stale approvals and erasure gaps.
modules.owns: Policy versions, delegation grants, consent/evidence, action authorizations, suppression and privacy-rights cases.

features.description: Typed action catalog with authority, required evidence, budget, tenant scope, expiry, policy version and exact permitted side effect.
Observe/recommend, draft/review and delegated-execution modes with explicit action grants; unknown/ungranted actions fail closed.
Candidate-captured purpose/job/client-scoped consent; notices, authenticity, expiry, withdrawal, channel preference and contact restrictions.
One suppression/eligibility API used by sourcing, AI, sharing, messaging, reminders, exports and workers; immediate withdrawal propagation.
Approval binds resource version, content digest, recipient, purpose and expiry; revalidate at execution, cancel stale approvals, prevent concurrent consumption.
features.implementation_note: W2 public follow-up controls and grants require the reviewed revision; edits and recovery never reuse a consumed delivery approval.

features.description: Privacy inventory/retention, export/correction/deletion, legal-hold exceptions, deletion tombstones, queue/result redaction and restartable erasure.
Jurisdiction/source rules, overseas recruitment and verification requirements, recording consent, sensitive-data minimization and documented agency/client/candidate authority.
Action-policy simulator and explanation; quiet-hour exceptions require explicit scoped policy, not hidden bypasses.

modules.accept: Withdrawal blocks queued sends/shares and pending decisions; all alternate routes enforce the same rules; deletion cannot be undone by parsing/replay; approval retries cannot double-execute.

modules.name: Durable workflow, scheduler aur workers
modules.baseline: Queue/retry code exists; stale locks, usage-write failures and mock schedules remain.
modules.owns: Workflow instances, event outbox, consumer inbox, durable timers, task leases and execution attempts.

features.description: Versioned workflow definitions, typed commands/events, transactional outbox/inbox, correlation IDs and per-candidacy/client/job/invoice process instances.
Real external scheduler or managed worker timer service; persistent timers survive deploys, browser closure and restarts; health verifies actual callbacks.
features.implementation_note: W3 due/grace/promise deadlines use the existing persistent queue and worker; production supervision and recovery drills remain open.

features.description: Atomic task claiming, leases/heartbeats, stale-running recovery, bounded concurrency, retry backoff/jitter, dead-letter queues and replay tools.

features.implementation_note: W3 collection source processing and financial facts are deterministic and continue with an exhausted AI budget.

features.description: Idempotent domain commands, timeout/compensation paths, cancellation propagation, version checks and reconciliation after unknown provider outcomes.
Fairness across workspaces, priority/deadline scheduling, rate limits, workflow migrations, pause/drain/resume and operation-level emergency stops.
M06 declares business follow-up deadlines; M05 alone persists/fires physical timers. No per-feature cron loops or competing next-run columns.
features.implementation_note: W3 reuses automationQueue for invoice/grace/promise deadlines; lastEvaluatedAt is a past-observation fairness cursor, not a second timer.

modules.accept: Kill a worker after claim and recover the job; event replay does not repeat an effect; a failed provider call never silently completes; no real timer means schedule not ready.

modules.name: Universal follow-up aur next-action management

features.description: One engine for prospect, proposal, consent, candidate response, screening, client feedback, interview, offer, joining, guarantee and collection follow-ups.

features.implementation_note: W3 adds owner-opted-in overdue invoice and missed-promise source adapters in review mode; most lifecycle adapters, pre-due reminders and regional holidays remain open.

features.description: Stop/pause/replan on reply, opt-out, bounce, withdrawal, accepted offer, paid invoice, role closure, reschedule, manual ownership or changed evidence.

features.description: Recipient-wide frequency caps and collision arbitration across jobs, campaigns, workspaces/accounts as permitted; merge compatible requests without leaking unrelated context.

Adaptive cadence from explicit preference/outcome data; out-of-office return-date handling, preferred channel, language, contact windows and escalation ladder.
Exactly one active logical follow-up per purpose/recipient/resource/version/step; retries preserve its identity; uncertain delivery enters reconciliation.
features.implementation_note: W3 prevents competing active invoice sequences across FU26/FU27, recipient changes and W2 edits; unresolved historic dispatches remain blocking.

features.description: Owner timeline: why due, goal, next action, expected stop condition, prior attempts, snooze/handoff, exhausted sequence and recovery options.
features.implementation_note: W2 adds explicit snooze, reviewed restarts, immutable definitions and recovery controls; broader handoff/adaptive cadence remains pending.

modules.accept: Reply/withdrawal/payment arriving just before dispatch cancels the stale attempt; reschedule replaces old timers; two modules cannot create duplicate nudges for the same purpose.

features.description: Unified email/portal/approved messaging inbox with person-company-job linkage, threading, attachments, assignments and authenticated reply capture.

Immutable approved sender/recipient/body/attachments digest, atomic dispatch claim, outbox, retries, provider idempotency where supported and uncertain-outcome reconciliation.
features.implementation_note: W2 supports owner-evidence resolution of uncertain completed attempts; provider-correlated automatic reconciliation and crash fencing remain pending.

features.description: Differentiate drafted, authorized, dispatching, provider_accepted, delivered, bounced, complained, replied and unknown; never infer delivered from send success.

modules.events: message.authorized, message.accepted, message.delivered, message.failed, message.replied, contact.opted_out
modules.accept: Complete request-approve-dispatch flow works; simultaneous delivery requests produce one logical send; duplicate receipts do not duplicate state; no leaked cross-tenant thread.
